entries.text: This test fails after changing the parser. What should I check first?

blocks.text: Compare the failing assertion with the new parser contract. Check the smallest input that reproduces the failure before changing either implementation.

entries.text: The empty-input case now returns an error instead of an empty result.

blocks.text: Confirm that the contract change is intentional. If it is, update that assertion and retain a test for a valid empty result. Otherwise, restore the previous behavior.

entries.text: Review a refactor that removes an allocation from a hot path.

blocks.text: Check buffer ownership, lifetime, and concurrency first. Removing an allocation is useful only if the replacement preserves those guarantees.

entries.text: What evidence would make you confident?

blocks.text: A focused correctness test, an explicit ownership contract, and before/after measurements using representative inputs on the target hardware.

entries.text: Suggest a regression test for accepting a packet with a missing header.

blocks.text: Use the shortest invalid packet and assert the public error result. Also keep one valid packet case.

entries.text: Can I treat this suggested test as verified?

blocks.text: Not yet. This is illustrative code: adapt it to the actual parser API and run it against both the buggy and fixed implementations.
